summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 4.I/577)

data.turoyo: Lo bas harke yaʕni. Aḥna kmətmanenawo aš šutosayḏan dəwewolən proġram d talawizyon dilonoyo.
data.translation: Not only here, that is. We used to wish that our institutions had their own television programme,

rationale: New Infectum-wa box, sustained institutional wish. Quote only the supplied verse, not the reader’s context expanded beyond that verse.

data.turoyo: Kmətmaneno b kul dukṯo aʕ ʕlayme w aʕ ʕlaymoṯo, d saymi hawxa ʕwodo. Dlo kloyo lazəm kulan d maltəmina am maʕlumat, d kit sas sowayḏan.
data.translation: I earnestly appeal to the young men and young women everywhere to do work like this. Without stopping, we must all gather the information that our elders have.

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell: ʕal-marked people with desired d-clause, within wishing rather than a separately established appeal sense.

data.translation: I wish you a pleasant and long life.

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell: recipient suffix -x and overt wished-for ḥaye contrast with the original implicit desired event.

data.turoyo: W lazəm mani yəlfina w ḥayrina laqəddam! W aḥna kmətmanena b kul darbo u ʕwodo d kətyo b kul darbo, d moṭe lu nišo kayiso yo.
data.translation: And we must learn and look ahead! And in every way we wish for the work that is being done in every way to reach the aim; it is good.

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell: first-person plural with desired event expressed by d-clause.

data.turoyo: I naqqa towe, kmətmaneno m Aloho d saymina fələm ḥalyo!
data.translation: When it happens, I hope to God that we make a nice film!

rationale: Fifth I Infectum example: m Aloho with desired d-clause adds a distinct participant frame.

summary: The zero-marked Armenian is the experiencer/subject, and the preceding invitation supplies what is desired. No overt dative experiencer or new complement frame is demonstrated.
The borrowed Arabic V shape is already filed as I in this glossary. Its source-language shape does not justify creating another Turoyo stem or a Detransitive.
No additional Idiomatic phrases or sense is supported by this repeated source context.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]. Appeal and hope are contextual English renderings; the published German sense remains sehnlichst wünschen.

The original entry and round 1 contain one Infectum example. Four selected Jan contexts bring that cell to five, varying recipient, desired NP, desired clause and divine participant. The overlapping first-person d-clause at 4.I/417 is not additionally added.
First-person plural kmətmanenawo adds Infectum-wa. It expresses a sustained institutional wish, not proof of repetitive wishing or any additional Detransitive morphology.
As in round 1, the Arabic V-shaped loan stays under the glossary’s I. Recipient -x in kmətmanenox does not establish an l-marked experiencer.
The reader’s context at Jan 4.I/577 continues beyond the supplied verse. The addition uses only the verse and its supplied English, without reconstructing or quoting the extra purpose clause.
Confirm the correspondence of prs 87/1 with PrS 34/52–53 before changing the existing source numbering.
Does ʕal people plus desired d-clause at Jan 2.1/3 conventionally mean an appeal/request, or is it an ordinary wish for their action? A separate sense is withheld.
Is m Aloho at Jan 4.I/430 an addressee/source of the requested outcome?
Desired content can be a d-clause, an overt life NP with recipient suffix, or an action of ʕal-marked people. m Aloho adds a divine participant. None alone proves a separate appeal sense.
